proposed_comments.title: Keep the haptic input window hidden until a wrap is pending
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep the haptic input window hidden until a wrap is pending

**Severity:** `high`

The new haptic route creates four topmost layered windows covering every virtual-screen edge and leaves them visible for the entire mouse-hook lifetime. Ordinary pointer movement at those edges can therefore hit the CursorWrap overlay instead of the underlying application or shell, even when no wrap is pending. Use a hidden, transient input window that is shown only at the actual wrap point, and hide it again as soon as the pending wrap completes or is cancelled.

confidence.rationale: The exact upstream head registers and shows all four WS_EX_TOPMOST edge windows at hook startup. The converged fork replaces them with a transient hidden window and the final fresh Copilot review returned zero new comments.

proposed_comments.body:
### Refresh haptic routing and preserve pending wraps across topology and device changes

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/MouseUtils/CursorWrap/dllmain.cpp`, especially `InitializeHaptics`, `OnDisplayChange`, `TryDeferWrapToHapticEdgeWindow`, `RegisterHapticEdgeWindows`, `CompletePendingHapticWrap`, and hook shutdown.

**Problem:** Haptic availability is sampled only when the listener starts, while the edge windows are built from the virtual-screen rectangle and the deferred wrap completes only if a later `WM_MOUSEMOVE` reaches one of those windows. Device hot-plug, display-layout changes, staggered monitor edges, window creation failure, or a missed mouse message can leave stale routing, skip haptic behavior, or leave `m_hasPendingWrap` set without completing the cursor move.

**Why it matters:** Cursor Wrap must preserve the configured cursor transition regardless of optional haptic support. A stale or missed haptic route can make wrapping stop working at valid monitor edges, intercept unrelated edge input, or leave the pending transition stuck after topology or device changes.

**Suggested change:**
1. Replace startup-only haptic initialization with a refresh routine that clears stale state, re-queries API/device availability, and cancels any pending wrap when haptics are unavailable.
2. Invoke that refresh from the existing display/device notification path after cancelling pending state and updating monitor topology.
3. Create one reusable hidden layered input window, move and show it only at the actual wrap point, and verify it owns the hit test before deferring the wrap.
4. Start a short timeout whenever a wrap is deferred; complete the pending cursor move from either `WM_MOUSEMOVE` or the timeout so optional haptic routing can never drop the wrap.
5. Centralize cancellation so it clears `m_hasPendingWrap`, kills the timeout, hides the input window, and is called during refresh and hook teardown.

**Verification:** Build the Debug x64 runner/settings essentials and `CursorWrap.vcxproj`. On staggered and indented multi-monitor layouts, verify wrapping completes at each real external edge while ordinary non-wrap edge movement reaches the underlying app or shell. Disconnect and reconnect the haptic device and change display topology while CursorWrap is active; verify availability refreshes, no stale overlay remains, and a missed input-window message still completes the pending cursor move through the timeout.

confidence.rationale: The exact upstream head samples haptic state once, constructs persistent windows from virtual-screen bounds, and has no timeout or centralized cancellation. The coordinated fork correction builds and converged with zero unresolved Copilot threads and zero new comments in the final review.
